items.stem: Why embed a live Jira query in a Confluence release page instead of pasting issue details by hand?

options.text: So the page stays in sync with the tracked issues and links do not rot
options.rationale: Correct: a live link keeps the page consistent with the source of truth.

options.text: Because it removes the need to review the notes
options.rationale: Review is still required regardless of linking.
Confluence displays text; the issue is drift, not capability.

items.explanation: Correct: a live link keeps the page consistent with the source of truth.
items.provenance: original Mastemy item drafted by an AI agent; no external question source

items.stem: Which TWO practices keep ChatGPT-drafted release notes trustworthy? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Verify each drafted line against its Jira issue
options.rationale: Correct: verification ties the note to the actual work record.

options.text: Use a consistent prompt template for structure
options.rationale: Correct: a template yields consistent, reviewable output.

options.text: Publish drafts before anyone reads them
options.rationale: Unreviewed drafts can misstate what shipped.

options.text: Invent issue keys that look plausible

items.explanation: Correct: verification ties the note to the actual work record.

items.stem: Jira comments contain useful context but are free text. What is the limitation for reporting?

options.text: Free text is not reliably queryable, so structured fields are needed for reporting
options.rationale: Correct: structured fields support consistent queries; comments do not.

options.text: Comments cannot be read by people
options.rationale: Comments are readable; they are just not queryable.
Consistent reporting relies on structured fields.

items.explanation: Correct: structured fields support consistent queries; comments do not.
